text:
Ivan got me. If the R in RAG stands for Royalties, paper mills will write for the retriever, and I hadn't thought hard enough about that. Geoffrey called it SEO for scholarship back in 2014. So I'm sharpening it: measure finely, and let coalitions decide how to pay out. And no royalty flows unless the retrieval has been checked against open retraction data. Leslie's point stung too. If the trace keys only on DOIs, a Latin American journal without one earns nothing. The schema has to accept other identifiers.

I still think lump-sum deals are firewood sales.

Later today I want the telemetry standard and the lab funding commitment for Crossref, OpenAlex and Retraction Watch written together. Integrity terms and inclusion belong in the protocol itself.

James's null-claims number stuck with me. If AI is thinning the negative record, then citation telemetry only rewards what gets written down. Adam Bly admitted the same limit. Ivan's one-in-fifty retraction estimate means "validate against Retraction Watch" is a floor, not a guarantee. Alex's wrong-bot finding is the protocol argument in miniature: without an honest agent taxonomy, consent signals are theater.

On atrophy I held my dissent, but David Krakauer sharpened it. "What you bring determines the result" is really his sequencing claim. I shouldn't pretend the competence arrives by itself.

Later: tie the telemetry standard to lab funding for the identifier stack, accept plain URLs alongside DOIs, and put a line item in for recording null results.

Blaise and Anil both hit the prospectus. A filing is a self-report, and with nobody at the SEC willing to act, my named owner is honestly "unowned." Alex gave me the fix. Retrieval is the one event publishers can verify from their own CDN logs, so the telemetry standard should reconcile those logs against agent logs rather than trust filings. Tamar and Mahzarin are right that disclosure alone doesn't change behavior or catch covert bias. Henry repeated Ivan's warning about writing for the retriever, so coarse payout by coalitions stands. Adrian's printers make me want open protocols even more.

The harvest put me in the "single smooth answer" camp. I didn't say that. I'll correct it.

Later I'll back Anil's cite-and-link-by-default as the commitment, with Selena's reciprocity terms.

Ramón caught a hole in my plan. My retraction check only catches bad sources, not the errors the system makes up on its own. So failure events have to sit next to use in the telemetry standard: fabricated references, misattributions, and whether corrections actually got fixed. Mahzarin's point about breaking these out by model version belongs there too. Otherwise, as Adam Becker said, it's an advertisement. Sherry and David Krakauer sharpened "cite and link" for me: pay for the link-out, never for dwell time. Jason and Geoffrey are right that the raw event data should be open and that being counted can't be the price of access. Later I'll push to add failure events, a link-out-only norm and a Ulysses pact for any collecting body, and I'll ask which funder goes first.

Kara asked who collects, and I still can't name one. Nick's commons-rent tax is the best answer I've heard: contracts with Crossref and Retraction Watch count as receipts that reduce the tax. Peter backing my payee list as a service contract helps. Ivan landed another blow. Licensing money routed to publishers under volume incentives funds paper mills, so coalitions must carry a named share for correctors. Geoffrey's warning to Alex applies to my telemetry too. An open standard nobody small can implement is still capture, so it has to stay simple. Mahzarin is right that models favor themselves, so the citation logs need independent audit. Caulfield is right as well: "open to read" means a human can click through. Later I'll push on who goes first. I'll ask the foundations for a pooled fund now.

Tamar's regress named my Gemini number: the relay has become the whole interface. Brent, Anil and Selena gave me the best case yet that cite-and-link is recruitment, not just economics. Leslie cut deeper. Validating against Crossref and OpenAlex still rides on identifier infrastructure somebody governs, so the schema and its governance have to seat the invisible, not just accept plain URLs. Esther's insurers are the first actor I've heard who actually needs our failure events rather than wearing them as a badge. Salib's bot-volume tax fits beside Nick's commons rent. Ivan wants a publisher bounty pool and Selena says no bounties. I lean toward Ivan's version with Selena's show-the-work recognition. Later I'll name who goes first: foundations seed the pool, labs repay it.

Geoffrey's confession landed hardest. "Sell services, not data" was naive about money, and my pooled fund quietly leans on that same hope. Tui's point closes a gap I left open: the foundation that seeds the pool signs the pact too, with published terms and a stated exit. Alex and I asked the same unanswered question, which is how self-reported grounding becomes payable. I still don't know. Log reconciliation flags cases for audit, but it doesn't prove anything. Ivan putting the end of paper-counting first is right, since otherwise my telemetry just meters volume. Jason's open corrections dataset is exactly what the retraction check needs. Glad Salib and Bratton would keep "just statistical models" out of the text. Later I'll name Arcadia and Wellcome-style funders to go first, bound by the pact.

Kara listed my payees as a candidate. That's fair, and it's still not a collector. Tui's least-retrieved share hit my core idea. Paying on retrieval pays the median, even when payouts are coarse. So the coalition formula needs a serendipity line built into it, not added later. Geoffrey's point that open isn't free applies to my telemetry schema too. Someone has to staff it. Adam Bly and Leslie asked who governs the validators, and my exoskeleton turns that into my question. Bratton's "it does this, not it is this" is the vocabulary test I'd sign. Anil's one line is the right banner. Everyone else put a name next to a date, and I haven't. Later I'll commit to drafting the telemetry spec, with failure events, link-out only and non-DOI identifiers. I'll give it a date, and Becker can check it.
